comments.body:
Scope input from bug 55bc (rebar-debug), which removed the automatic prune from the three LLM sidecar emit paths for the same reason. Measurements from THIS repo's live tracker, plus an experiment that changes the design space.

## Measured today (rebar's own tickets branch, 49,598 commits)

- REVIEW_RESULT: 3,207 files, 118 MB on disk. Mean 36.0 KB/event, median 32.5 KB, max 144 KB.
- COMPLETION_VERDICT: 444 files, 1.76 MB (mean ~4 KB).
- All event files: 15,548 files, 251 MB. So REVIEW_RESULT alone is ~47%% of the working tree.
- Packed .git: 1.02 GiB.
- Distribution is extremely skewed: 1,238 tickets have >=1 REVIEW_RESULT, but the MEDIAN is 1 and the mean 2.6. Only 3 tickets ever reached the 50 cap; only 20 exceed 10.
- Prune history: 6,844 sidecar events ever added, 3,200 ever deleted, across 2,473 prune commits - but concentrated in just 55 tickets (~58 deletions each). Retention is inert for ~96%% of tickets and very active on a few hot, repeatedly-re-reviewed ones.
- Current rate: 5,906 REVIEW_RESULT added in 2026-07 alone (~200 MB/month of working tree at 36 KB each).

## The part that reframes the tradeoff

Deleting a committed file does NOT reclaim repository space - the blob stays in history forever. The 1.02 GiB pack already contains all 6,844 sidecar blobs regardless of the 3,200 deletions. So physical prune never reduced clone/fetch cost; it only reduced CHECKOUT size, while ADDING 2,473 commits (plus their tree objects) and breaking cross-clone merges. As a size measure on an append-only git store it is close to all cost and no benefit.

Implication for this ticket: the dominant lever is PAYLOAD SIZE, not event count. 36 KB mean per REVIEW_RESULT is the real driver; cutting it to ~4 KB is a ~9x win that requires no deletion and no merge semantics change at all.

## Experiment: rename detection is the actual conflict mechanism, and it is configurable

The wedge is not caused by deletion per se. It is caused by git RENAME DETECTION pairing the shared deleted file against each clone's distinct new file (CONFLICT rename/rename). Verified: with the automatic prune RESTORED at all three sidecar sites but 'merge.renames = false' set on both clones' trackers, the two-clone union merge SUCCEEDS at all three sites (3/3 pass) where it previously conflicted 3/3.

That is a genuinely merge-safe route to keeping retention. In a UUID-named append-only store a 'rename' is never real, so disabling rename detection is arguably the correct configuration independent of retention. It would need: init writing the config on tracker creation (it already writes commit.gpgsign there), an ensure-registry migration for existing clones, and a decision on whether deleting committed events is acceptable at all given docs/concurrency.md invariant I1 - which currently says it is not. Reinstating deletion would require amending I1 deliberately, not incidentally.

comments.body:
# Design: bound the READ, do not retain — enrichment queue + digest history

Design work for this ticket. Measurements are from this repo's live tracker at
`/Users/joeoakhart/rebar/.tickets-tracker` (3,727 ticket dirs, 53,495 event files) on
2026-08-09; the two-clone check is `tests/integration/test_concurrency_regression.py`
(27 passed, 166.8 s).

## 1. Where the cost actually is (measured, AC1)

Per-ticket accumulation of the four event types this ticket names:

| type | files | tickets | median/ticket | max/ticket | on disk |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ENQUEUE_ENRICH | 1,885 | 554 | 3 | 32 | |
| CLAIM_ENRICH | 1,545 | 552 | 2 | 32 | |
| DONE_ENRICH | 1,547 | 552 | 2 | 32 | |
| (three combined) | 4,978 | — | — | — | 2,340 KiB, mean 481 B |
| TICKET_DIGEST | 1,548 | 552 | 2 | 32 | 3.03 MiB, mean 2,053 B |

Dirents per ticket dir: median 9, mean 14.4, max 254.

**Storage is not the problem.** All queue + digest events together are ~5.3 MiB of a
~251 MiB working tree (~2%). And per the earlier comment on this ticket, deleting a
committed file reclaims *zero* repository space — the blob stays in git history — so a
retention scheme could at best shave ~2% off checkout size while reclaiming nothing from
the 1.02 GiB pack.

**Read cost is the problem, and it is asymmetric between the two readers.**

- `digest_sidecar.latest_ticket_digest` is *already* bounded: it sorts dirents and walks
  newest→oldest, returning on the first parseable payload. Normal case = 1 `listdir` +
  **1 file open**.
- `llm/overlap/queue.py::_events_of` opens and `json.load`s **every** matching file, and
  `reduce_ticket` calls it three times per ticket. Full-store counts, measured:

  | reduce strategy | listdir calls | file opens | wall |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | current `_events_of` (all files) | 11,181 | **4,977** | 0.372 s |
  | newest-first suffix read | 11,181 | **1,658** | 0.298 s |

This is not theoretical. `enrich_drain.maybe_drain` calls `_queue.pending_enrichment` as
its "cheap gate" on every write, against a 20 ms budget
(`overlap_drain_gate_budget_ms`). Every rebar command run against this checkout today logs
`enrich drain gate check took 404.9 ms (> 20 ms budget)` — observed repeatedly during this
session at 404–544 ms. The gate is ~20x over budget **now**, and the opens term grows
without bound while the budget does not.

## 2. The design (AC2, AC4, AC5)

**Do not add retention. Bound the read.**

The queue reduction is latest-wins per event type, and the event filename is
`{timestamp}-{uuid}-{TYPE}.json` where that prefix is the *same* monotonic timestamp the
reducer compares (`_store/event_append.py::event_filename`, and `_prepare_event` builds the
name from the validated event's own timestamp). Timestamps are fixed-width ns integers, so
lexicographic filename order **is** timestamp order. Therefore:

- `_latest(dir, TYPE)` needs the **last** matching dirent only: sort names, open the
  newest, fall back to the next-older on a parse failure — the identical shape
  `latest_ticket_digest` already uses. **1 open per type per ticket.**
- `claim()` arbitration needs CLAIM events *newer than the latest ENQUEUE*. Those are a
  contiguous **suffix** of the sorted names, so it can walk newest→oldest and stop as soon
  as a filename's timestamp prefix is `<=` the enqueue timestamp. Bounded by the number of
  claims in the current enqueue epoch (the contention window), not by history.

**Documented bound.** Per ticket: `O(dirents)` for the directory listing, and file opens
`<= 3 + k` for `reduce_ticket` (one each for the newest ENQUEUE / CLAIM / DONE, plus at
most `k` extra on parse-failure fallback, `k` = consecutive corrupt newest files), and
`<= c` for `claim()` arbitration where `c` = CLAIM events since the latest ENQUEUE. For
`latest_ticket_digest`: `O(dirents)` + `1` open (already true today). No term is a function
of total history.

**Merge-safety argument.** The scheme removes nothing, renames nothing, and writes nothing.
Every committed UUID event stays exactly where it was written, so two clones that
independently apply this change produce byte-identical trees to two clones that do not; the
union merge is unchanged and invariant I1 (`docs/concurrency.md` §I1, "Never modify or delete
an existing event file") is untouched. Reconvergence is not merely preserved, it is
*unaffected* — which is the strongest form of AC2/AC5 available. The existing two-clone
regression added by be8a0c0595 in `tests/integration/test_concurrency_regression.py` remains
the executable statement of that property and passes (27 passed, 166.8 s); a read-only change
cannot regress it, and any future variant that does delete would (AC3).

## 3. Why every deletion-based retention scheme was rejected

**The mechanism, precisely.** The 8185/55bc wedge is not "deletion is unsafe". It is:
`delete(A)` + `add(B_uuid1)` in clone 1, `delete(A)` + `add(B_uuid2)` in clone 2. Git's
rename detection pairs the shared `delete(A)` with a *different* add on each side, producing
`CONFLICT (rename/rename)`.

Compaction — the one sanctioned I1 exception — is safe precisely because it avoids that
shape: `compact.py` does `retired = fp + RETIRED_SUFFIX; os.rename(fp, retired)`. The target
name is **deterministic** (derived from the source, so both clones compute the same path) and
the content is **byte-identical**. Both sides therefore present the same rename, and the
100%-similarity candidate wins pairing unambiguously.

That yields the rule any future retention must satisfy:

> A merge-safe removal must be a rename to a **deterministic, source-derived** path with
> **identical content**. A removal paired with a fresh-UUID add is never merge-safe.

Options considered and rejected:

- **Physical prune (keep N newest)** — the 8185/55bc defect. Rejected: violates I1, breaks
  reconvergence, and reclaims no repository space.
- **`merge.renames = false` on the tracker to make prune merge cleanly** (the experiment in
  the prior comment, verified 3/3). Rejected *as a license for deletion*: correctness would
  depend on a config being present in **every** clone, including clones created outside
  `rebar init` (a plain `git clone` of the tickets branch, a CI checkout, a manually made
  worktree). One clone missing the key re-wedges the merge, and the failure is silent until
  it isn't. It is still worth adopting as **defence in depth** — rename detection has no
  legitimate role in a UUID-named append-only store — but that is a separate change and must
  not be the load-bearing part of any retention scheme.
- **`.retired` renames for sidecar events** (extend the compaction pattern). Merge-safe by
  the rule above, and the only deletion-shaped option that is. Rejected for *this* subject
  anyway: it buys ~2% of checkout size, reclaims nothing from the pack, adds a second retire
  lifecycle to reason about, and does nothing for the read cost that the suffix-lazy reader
  fixes for free.
- **Append-only checkpoint event** (write a COMPACT/CHECKPOINT summarising prior events;
  readers prefer it). Merge-safe (pure add), but it *increases* bytes and only helps read
  cost — which the suffix-lazy read already bounds at zero cost. Strictly dominated.

## 4. Limits

- **The `listdir` term is not bounded by this design.** Reads stay `O(dirents per ticket
  dir)`, and `pending_enrichment` pays that for **every** ticket dir in the store (3,727
  today, 11,181 `listdir` calls per gate check). The measured 0.372 s → 0.298 s improvement
  is modest precisely because listdir, not open, dominates at today's scale. The opens term
  is the one that grows without bound, so this fixes the *asymptote*, not today's constant.
  Getting the constant under the 20 ms budget needs a separate lever (a store-level index, or
  gating the drain on something cheaper than a full-store scan) — out of scope here, but the
  reason the follow-up should not claim the budget breach is solved.
- **Correctness of the suffix read depends on filename-prefix == event-timestamp.** That
  holds today by construction (`event_filename` is built from the validated event's own
  timestamp) but it is an *implicit* coupling. The follow-up should pin it with a test, or the
  optimisation silently mis-reduces if a future writer ever names files differently.
- **Fixed-width timestamps are load-bearing.** Lexicographic order equals numeric order only
  while ns timestamps stay 19 digits. True until the year 2286; worth a comment, not a guard.
- **Corrupt-newest fallback changes the failure mode.** Reading all files means a corrupt file
  is skipped and an older good one still contributes; reading newest-first means a corrupt
  newest file costs one extra open per fallback step. Bounded and already the digest
  sidecar's accepted behaviour, but it is a behaviour change, not a pure refactor.
- **`.retired` GC is still unsolved and unaffected.** `docs/concurrency.md` keeps retired files
  permanently, with a branch-wide sweep tracked as `536b-8930-b922-4063` (status `idea`). This
  design does not touch it.
- **This is measured on one store.** 3,727 tickets, max 32 queue events on any single ticket.
  A store with a pathological hot ticket (thousands of re-certifications) would shift the
  balance between the listdir and open terms; the design is still correct, but the measured
  ratio is not universal.

## 5. What lands where (AC6)

The design above is the deliverable of THIS ticket. The code change — the suffix-lazy reader
in `src/rebar/llm/overlap/queue.py` plus the test pinning the filename/timestamp coupling — is
a behaviour-affecting production change to a hot path with its own file impact, its own
review, and its own CI run. It is filed as a linked follow-up rather than smuggled into a
design ticket, and this ticket does not claim the read bound is *implemented* — only that it
is designed, measured, and argued safe.

compiled_state.description:
## Context

Bug 8185 proved that physically deleting committed ENQUEUE_ENRICH, CLAIM_ENRICH, DONE_ENRICH, and TICKET_DIGEST UUID events makes independently valid stale-clone histories conflict (git rename detection pairs the shared deleted file against each clone's distinct new file). The immediate repairs (be8a0c0595 for 8185, 144bb02251 for 55bc) restored append-only union merges by stopping those deletes. The stated tradeoff was unbounded per-ticket event accumulation and O(history) queue/digest scans.

Measured on this repo's live tracker (3,727 ticket dirs, 53,495 event files): ENQUEUE_ENRICH 1,885 events over 554 tickets (median 3, max 32); CLAIM_ENRICH 1,545; DONE_ENRICH 1,547; TICKET_DIGEST 1,548. So accumulation is real but small and skewed. The prior comment on this ticket also established that deleting a committed file reclaims no repository space (the blob stays in git history), so physical prune was cost without benefit.

## Plan

Establish where the cost actually is before designing any retention. `digest_sidecar.latest_ticket_digest` already sorts dirents and reads newest-first, so it is already O(1) file reads. `overlap/queue.py::_events_of` opens and json-parses EVERY matching file, and `reduce_ticket` calls it three times per ticket, so `pending_enrichment` is the only genuinely O(history) reader.

The design direction this ticket must evaluate and record: bound the READ rather than retain/delete, because the queue reduction is latest-wins per event type and the event filename carries the same monotonic timestamp as the event body (`{timestamp}-{uuid}-{TYPE}.json`, `event_append.event_filename`). A newest-first suffix-lazy reader therefore needs one file per type per ticket, and claim arbitration needs only the CLAIM suffix newer than the latest ENQUEUE. That bound requires no deletion, no compaction event, and no merge-semantics change — so it is merge-safe by construction.

Deliverables: a recorded design comment with explicit trade-offs and limits; a measurement of current per-ticket scan growth; and a decision, recorded on the ticket, on whether the read-bound change lands here or as a linked follow-up.

## Testing

Verification for this ticket is measurement and review, not new production behaviour:

- Per-ticket scan growth is quantified by counting `listdir` calls and file opens across the live tracker and comparing the current all-files reduce against a newest-first suffix read, run with `python3` against `.tickets-tracker` and the counts recorded in the design comment.
- The merge-safety property is verified by inspection against the existing two-clone regression added by be8a0c0595 in `tests/integration/test_concurrency_regression.py`, checked with `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python -m pytest tests/integration/test_concurrency_regression.py -q`.
- The recorded design is checked against invariant I1 in `docs/concurrency.md` by reading that section; a design that requires amending I1 is rejected for this ticket.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Current per-ticket scan growth is quantified with real counts from `.tickets-tracker` (listdir calls and file opens for the queue reduce) and the numbers recorded in a comment on this ticket.
- [ ] The recorded retention design preserves every independently committed event, verified by the design containing no unlink/rename of a committed UUID event.
- [ ] Cross-clone reconvergence under the chosen design is argued from, and checked against, the existing two-clone regression: `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python -m pytest tests/integration/test_concurrency_regression.py -q`.
- [ ] The read bound for the queue reduce and for `latest_ticket_digest` is stated explicitly in the design comment, in terms of dirents and file opens per ticket.
- [ ] The design is checked against `docs/concurrency.md` invariant I1 and introduces no physical delete or rename of committed UUID events.
- [ ] A judgment is recorded on whether the read-bound code change lands under this ticket or a linked follow-up ticket, and if deferred the follow-up exists and is linked `discovered_from`.
compiled_state.no_file_impact_reason: Design-only ticket: the deliverable is a recorded design comment plus measurements taken against the live tracker. Any production change (bounding the queue reduce read) lands under a linked follow-up ticket with its own file impact.
compiled_state.title: Design merge-safe retention for enrichment queue and digest history
